In Blocker settings, look for “Block when tasks are due within.” Choose the window that fits your day and make sure blocking is enabled. A task due next week should not be treated like a task due shortly unless your selected window includes it.

Make time to do the task
Menu wording can vary with your app version and language. Keep essential communication, navigation and emergency tools accessible when choosing distractions to block.
Neither version is intended as tamper-proof device management. Permissions, available break actions and operating-system settings affect what can be blocked. You remain in control of those settings.

No. A daily usage limit responds to how long you use an app. Nonlate’s deadline-aware blocking responds to unfinished due work. If you only need a fixed daily usage cap, your phone’s built-in screen-time controls may be enough.
No. Blocking adds friction before a distraction; it does not do the task for you. Pair it with a small next action and a realistic work session. Avoid treating an app as a guarantee of productivity.
No. Calendar events appear in Schedule but do not trigger blocking. Nonlate checks eligible unfinished tasks and their deadlines instead.

Open one of your selected distracting apps while an unfinished task qualifies for blocking. Return to the work, or use a supported timed break when appropriate. Optional Focus Lock removes the quick-break button from the blocker; a break can still be started from Home inside Nonlate after a due-task check and reflection pause.

Try one task and one distraction
Use Planner and Schedule to choose when to work. Planning a task does not change its deadline, and a calendar event is not a blocking task.

Use an app blocker that checks unfinished tasks, not just a timer. In Nonlate, you choose distracting apps and a due-work window. When a selected app opens while an eligible task is overdue or due within that window, Nonlate blocks access with the presentation supported by your device.
